$comment: Coverage floors and the settings that decide what each floor measures. This file is the source of truth; each manifest below carries a copy that its test runner reads, and scripts/check-coverage-thresholds-sync.ts fails when a copy differs. jest.<package> mirrors the jest block of <package>/package.json: every key but the few that cannot move a floor (JEST_FREE_KEYS in the script), so a key added to the block has to be added here. pytest.agent.run and .report mirror [tool.coverage.run] and [tool.coverage.report] in agent/pyproject.toml, whole, and give the coverage flags of the test task in agent/mise.toml; pytest.agent.addopts is addopts of [tool.pytest.ini_options] there, verbatim, because pytest puts it in front of that task's command line. vitest.web mirrors the test block of web/vite.config.ts in the same way (VITEST_FREE_KEYS). commands gives scripts.test of each package.json verbatim: it is the command the build runs, and a flag there wins over the settings pinned here. tasks gives the mise task that runs each of those scripts and the agent's pytest, named as mise names it (//<directory>:<task>, in <directory>/mise.toml): every key but description and depends (TASK_FREE_KEYS), because what follows the script's name on a task line reaches the runner too. node:test has no config file, so the floors of integrations/jira-forge-app are the --test-coverage flags of its script. Raise a floor when coverage improves; do not lower a floor or narrow a scope without maintainer approval. cdk floors measured 2026-06-02; cli and agent floors set 2026-11-10 from CI build 42716472700; web floors set 2026-11-11 two points under a local macOS run (90.81 / 82.6 / 91.11 / 93.36), because CI does not measure web coverage yet; jira-forge-app floors set the same day two points under 87.50 / 78.87 / 83.33 (lines, branches, functions), measured locally with Node 22.22.3.
